title: Absolute Value: Distance from Zero
preview: Anchor on |5| = 5. Vary signs and contexts until 'absolute value is the distance from zero' emerges from the pattern.

body.goal: Students articulate absolute value as distance from zero on the number line — by working through deliberately varied cases that surface the always-positive result and the opposite-of-opposite return.
body.launch: Sketch a number line and mark 0. Don't define absolute value out loud — just write the symbol and ask groups to predict the answers. The pattern they invent IS the definition.
body.prerequisiteLabel: Warm up: locate numbers and their opposites.

prerequisiteSteps.teacherNote: Opposite of a negative is a positive.

prerequisiteSteps.problem: How far is 5 from 0 on a number line?

steps.teacherNote: Vary one thing: the sign. The answer didn't change — push why.
Edge case — zero distance from zero.
Vary type — works with fractions too.
Subtle — the negative is OUTSIDE the absolute-value bars. Take absolute value first, then negate.
Same — |−5| = 5 first, then negate. Pushes the order of operations.
Take each absolute value first, then add.
Vary structure: now the absolute value is on the SUM. Compute inside first.

enrichmentSteps.teacherNote: Sum inside first: −10. Then |−10| = 10. Different answer.

body.consolidation: Bring the class back. Ask: 'In one sentence — what does the absolute value bars MEAN?' Push for 'distance from zero on the number line.' Then: 'Why is |−5| = 5 the same as |5|?' (Distance doesn't care about direction.) Finally compare steps 11 and 12 — why are |−4| + |3| and |−4 + 3| different?
